findings.detail: The head text of `docs/operations/model-migration.md` (lines 142-145) now says `HandleRegisterModel` only validates manifest identity and inventory and checks listed file sizes. It adds that 'Providers verify the actual file hashes when downloading.' The base text (lines 137-138) said the coordinator verified every listed file's existence, size and hash. If this reflects a real backend change, publication-time integrity checking has moved from the trusted coordinator to adversarial providers. A bad or tampered CDN/R2 object, or a manifest that does not match the files, would then be caught only on provider devices. A malicious provider (ADV-001) can skip that check and serve substituted weights (T-012, T-027, A-004). The new step 1 text also lets operators reuse already-published files without re-upload. Nothing in the supplied threat model records that the coordinator stopped checking hashes. Update the weight-substitution threats and mitigations to state the new verification point. Also state that the registered manifest hashes remain the trust anchor for provider downloads. If the hash check was removed unintentionally, restore it. The backend code is out of scope here, so this is unconfirmed.
findings.title: Registration docs now say the coordinator no longer verifies file hashes; the model-integrity threats are not updated
